$comment: The one home of knobly's diagnostic codes. spec/spec.md 2.4's table is generated from this file (tools/gen-api.py docs). 'layer' owns the code: syntax (parse), written (the low level: the graph's diagnostics, spec 6.3; the expanded value's readers, spec 2.9), include (the include extension). 'found by' is from a closed list: parse, edit (a bad text error's diagnostics), load and read, low level (worked out from the current texts), readers, include extension. 'message' is the base message (a binding may append ': <detail>'; messages are for people, spec 2.3); '{nesting depth}' names the limit of that name in api.json. 'unreadable reason' is the reason of the statement the code makes unreadable, null when it never does (readers raise it). 'meaning' (the spec's), 'summary' and 'placed at' (the user guide's, docs/site/pages/diagnostics.md) are Markdown; both tables are generated from this file. In 'meaning' and 'summary' write a limit as '{limit name}', which the generated tables fill with its value (100,000); writing the value by hand is refused (tools/gen-api.py), so api.json stays the value's one home.

retired.now: nothing: a line break is whitespace, so a '{' may start its line (owner, 2026-10-29, Q1)
E1005, found by parse (the BAD_ESCAPE error token)

rules: Codes are stable across bindings and releases and are never reused for another meaning.
Every code is an error; there are no warning codes.
A program's own codes are '<namespace>/<name>' (api.json patterns, program code) and never collide with these.

codes.name: unterminated string
codes.meaning: A string reaches the end of its line or of the text without its closing quote.
codes.summary: a string with no closing quote

codes.name: unexpected character
codes.meaning: A character no token may start with, or a byte-order mark after the first character.
codes.summary: a character the language does not use

codes.name: lone dollar
codes.message: '$' must be followed by a variable name
codes.meaning: A `$` not followed by a variable name.
codes.summary: `$` not followed by a name

codes.name: bad escape
codes.meaning: A closed double-quoted string holding a backslash escape other than the six (the `BAD_ESCAPE` error token), placed on the string. A single-quoted string is raw: it has no escapes.
codes.summary: a double-quoted string escape other than the six (found by the parser; a single-quoted string is raw)

codes.name: unexpected token
codes.meaning: A token the grammar does not allow here, when no more specific code applies: among them the end of the text at the top level, or a `}`, where a directive's `;` or block is due (3.2). Also an edit's bad text error, from its entry rule (2.8): at the first token the entry rule does not allow, or at the end of the text.
codes.summary: a token where it cannot go, a missing `;` at the end of a block or file among them

codes.name: expected closing brace
codes.meaning: The text ends inside a block: reported once, at the end of the text, however many blocks are open; not after a statement whose error runs to the end of the text, and not inside an open `[` (E2004) (3.2).
codes.summary: a block with no `}`

codes.name: expected closing bracket
codes.meaning: A stray `]`, or a `[` list with no matching `]`.
codes.summary: an unmatched bracket

codes.name: bad slice
codes.meaning: A malformed slice after a slice name (a word or a `$name`): `a[~]`, `a[1~b c]`, an unclosed slice, or a literal bound that is not an integer (`a[i]`, `a[1.5]`, `a[1:3]`, whose `1:3` is one word).
codes.summary: a malformed slice (`[~]` among them, and `[1:3]`, whose `1:3` is one word), or a literal bound that is not a whole number

codes.name: values touch
codes.message: values must be separated by a space or comment
codes.meaning: Two values with nothing between them, such as `a"b"`.
codes.summary: two values with no space or comment between

codes.name: nesting too deep
codes.message: blocks and lists nest deeper than {nesting depth} levels
codes.meaning: Blocks and lists nested deeper than {nesting depth} levels. Also an edit's bad text error when the document after the edit would nest past it (2.8).
codes.summary: blocks and lists nested deeper than {nesting depth}
codes.placed at: the `{` or `[` that opens the level past the limit; at an edit, 0:0 when that bracket is not in the given text

codes.name: include not found
codes.meaning: An extension's spec matched no file.
codes.summary: a spec matched no file

codes.name: include resolver failed
codes.meaning: The document source rejected while resolving or reading a file. For the root file, `load` fails instead (6.2).
codes.summary: the source threw (for the root file `load` fails)

codes.name: include bad path
codes.meaning: An `include` whose values are not exactly one quoted path.
codes.summary: include needs exactly one quoted path
codes.placed at: the bad value, or the name when there is none

codes.name: extension failed
codes.meaning: An extension threw something other than a diagnostic error, or returned something other than a list of texts.
codes.summary: an extension threw something other than a located error, or returned something other than a list of texts

codes.name: unread copy
codes.meaning: An extension line's copy whose specs are not resolved or whose files are not read yet (it is in `unread ()`); `read ()` reads them. Placed on the extension line's name.
codes.summary: an include copy whose files are not read yet (`graph.read()` reads them)

codes.name: unknown extension
codes.meaning: A statement written `@name` where `name` is no language statement (`set`, `snippet`, `use`) and no registered extension's name. Placed on the `@name`; the statement is an `unreadable line`.
codes.summary: an `@name` that is no language statement and no registered extension

codes.name: non-integer bound
codes.meaning: A slice or index bound reached through a variable that is not one integer word, or a literal integer beyond the integer range. A literal bound that is not an integer is E2007, found by parse.
codes.summary: a bound from a variable that is not one whole number, or a literal whole number beyond the range
codes.placed at: the bound (a bound from a variable: the value, via the variable)

codes.name: wrong value kind
codes.meaning: A reader asked for a kind the value is not.
codes.summary: a reader met the wrong kind of value

codes.name: not a number
codes.meaning: A word read as a number that is not a JSON number, or one beyond the double range (`1e400`; contract 2).
codes.summary: `number()` met a word that is not a number

codes.name: not an integer
codes.meaning: A word read as an integer that is not one, or one beyond plus or minus 2^53-1.
codes.summary: `integer()` met a word that is not a whole number

codes.name: not a boolean
codes.meaning: A word other than `true` or `false`, read as a boolean.
codes.summary: `boolean()` met a word other than `true`, `false`

codes.name: bad slice name
codes.message: slice name is not one word
codes.meaning: A slice or index whose name is a `$name` that does not hold exactly one `WORD` or `AT_WORD`, the words the grammar's `sliceName` takes (`$src[0~3]` with `$src` a string, a list, two values, or a number-like word such as `5`, `1.5`, `-` or `07:30`); placed as E4001 is.
codes.summary: a slice's `$name` that does not hold one word

codes.name: unknown variable
codes.meaning: A `$name` with no `set` visible and no override.
codes.summary: `$name` with no `set`, parameter or override

codes.name: variable set twice
codes.message: variable set twice in one block
codes.meaning: Two `set` lines for one name in one block.
codes.summary: two `set` of one name in one block

codes.name: unknown snippet
codes.meaning: A `use` naming no visible snippet.
codes.summary: `use` of a snippet not seen there

codes.name: snippet arity
codes.message: wrong number of values for the snippet
codes.meaning: A `use` with a different number of values than its snippet's parameters.
codes.summary: wrong number of values for the snippet

codes.name: snippet defined twice
codes.message: snippet defined twice in one block
codes.meaning: Two `snippet` lines for one name in one block.
codes.summary: two snippets of one name in one block

codes.name: expansion cycle
codes.meaning: A `use` or extension line that reaches itself again.
codes.summary: a snippet or file reaches itself
codes.placed at: the `@use` or extension line that closes the loop

codes.name: expansion too deep
codes.meaning: `use` and extension lines nested deeper than {expansion depth}.
codes.summary: more than {expansion depth} snippets or files open inside each other

codes.name: too many directives
codes.meaning: More than {directives} directives after expansion.
codes.summary: more than {directives} directives after expansion; expansion stops
codes.placed at: the statement that is one too many

codes.name: bad set
codes.meaning: A `set` line that is not `@set $name value...;`.
codes.summary: any other form of `@set`

codes.name: bad snippet
codes.meaning: A malformed `snippet` line (`@snippet name $p... { ... }`), or one naming a parameter twice.
codes.summary: any other form of `@snippet`

codes.name: bad use
codes.meaning: A `use` line that is not `@use name value...;`.
codes.summary: any other form of `@use`

codes.name: extension block not set
codes.message: an extension's block holds only @set lines
codes.meaning: An extension line whose block holds a line other than `@set`.
codes.summary: an extension line's block holds a line other than `@set`

codes.name: expanded nesting too deep
codes.message: expanded blocks and lists nest deeper than {expanded nesting depth}
codes.meaning: Blocks and lists nested deeper than {expanded nesting depth} levels after expansion (2.5): a directive whose block or values, or a `set`, `use` or extension line whose values, would sit deeper. The statement is unreadable there and its block is not walked.
codes.summary: blocks and lists nested deeper than {expanded nesting depth} after expansion
codes.placed at: the name of the statement whose block or values sit too deep
